ca_echo_cove_south_side.blurb: A busy cluster of short faces on the south flank of the cove at Echo Rock, in the middle of Joshua Tree National Park. The rock is vertical to a touch overhanging with flat ground at the base, which makes setting up top-ropes easy, and most lines can be led as well. Of the 16 routes, most are trad with a few bolted lines, running from about 5.7 up to a single 5.12. The bulk sit in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, so it suits intermediate to strong climbers more than beginners. The face stays shaded for most of the day, especially in winter, which helps in warm weather.

ca_hideout_west.blurb: One of three small crags that make up the Hideout, a scatter of low formations in the Alabama Hills outside Lone Pine in the Eastern Sierra. Hideout West is the westernmost of the rock clusters there and holds 16 routes, mostly bolted, with a handful of trad lines and two top-ropes. Difficulty is friendly: plenty of climbs fall between 5.6 and 5.9, with a few 5.10s to step up to. The surrounding area has a mix of north- and south-facing rock, so something is usually comfortable whatever the season. It makes a good short day for newer leaders.

ca_lower_freeway_wall.blurb: The lower tier of Freeway Wall in the Lost Horse area of Joshua Tree National Park, close to the dirt road. Every one of the 16 routes here is listed as trad, and the grades are gentle: a few scrambly lines, then a spread of 5.6 to 5.9, a handful of 5.10s and a single 5.11. That makes it a reasonable spot for newer climbers and for a warm-up before heading to the harder upper wall. Boulders scattered below the cliff make the short walk in a bit awkward, so wear sturdy shoes.

ca_6_franosch.blurb: A small cliff in the Silver Lake area above June Lake, in the Eastern Sierra at roughly 7,400 feet. The wall is only about 30 to 50 feet tall, and the quartzite is mixed, with some loose pieces, so keep belayers back and helmets on. Most of the 16 routes are set up as top-ropes, with a couple of bolted lines, an aid route and an easy scramble option. Grades are low, mainly 5.3 to 5.7 with a few harder pitches up to 5.10. It faces east-northeast, so mornings are the pleasant time, and it is a good place for beginners and quiet days.
ca_6_franosch.approach: From the Silver Lake trailhead, bear left at the junction and climb steeply uphill for a short distance.

ca_1_poison_garden.blurb: The first wall you meet on the trail at Marble Caves, a limestone ridge high over the Trinity River's South Fork in far northwest California. It holds 16 routes, most of them bolted with a few trad lines, ranging from 5.7 up to 5.12. The grades lean hard: twelve of the climbs are 5.10 or above, with a block of 5.12s, though the wall also offers a few easier warm-ups. It takes sun for most of the day, so it is best outside the hot months. Poison oak grows at the base, so watch where you stand and keep gear off the plants.
ca_1_poison_garden.approach: It is the first wall reached on the trail, about 10 to 15 minutes from the parking area.

ca_outward_bound_slab.blurb: A slab in the north end of the Wonderland of Rocks in Joshua Tree National Park, known as a quieter corner away from the busier cliffs. The 16 routes are almost all trad, with two top-ropes. Difficulty runs from very easy to 5.10, but most lines fall in the 5.4 to 5.8 band, so it is well suited to climbers building up their crack and slab skills. The slab catches strong sun, and the sun gets intense by midday, so it pays to start early and bring plenty of water. The granite is coarse and grippy.

ca_moosedog_tower.blurb: A prominent tower among the formations of Indian Cove, in the north of Joshua Tree National Park, with longer outings than most nearby rocks. Nearly all of the 16 routes are trad, with one bolted line, and many are two pitches on well-featured faces. Grades span roughly 5.6 to 5.10, with the largest share at 5.7 and 5.8, so there is plenty for newer trad leaders as well as a few harder lines. The south side takes the sun, so early or late in the day is more comfortable in warm weather. A rappel from the top returns you to the ground.
